Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows opacity confined to the right lung, with the later image (Figure 4), there is a clear increase in the right-sided opacity and the appearance of new opacities in the left lung. This progressive, multifocal pattern of consolidation is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can present with pneumonia-like infiltrates that spread over time.
